refs.quote: GLUMETZA is indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

The recommended starting dose of GLUMETZA is 500 mg orally once daily with the evening meal. • Increase the dose in increments of 500 mg every 1 to 2 weeks on the basis of glycemic control and tolerability, up to a maximum of 2,000 mg once daily with the evening meal.

dose.frequency: once daily with the evening meal; titrate by 500 mg every 1 to 2 weeks

regimens.dose_text: Starting dose: 500 mg orally once daily with the evening meal. Increase in increments of 500 mg every 1 to 2 weeks based on glycemic control and tolerability, up to a maximum of 2,000 mg once daily with the evening meal. Patients receiving metformin HCl tablets may switch to GLUMETZA once daily at the same total daily dose up to 2,000 mg/day. Swallow whole; never crush, cut, or chew.

refs.quote: GLUMETZA is contraindicated in patients with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) below 30 mL/minute/1.73 m 2 . • Initiation of GLUMETZA in patients with an eGFR between 30 to 45 mL/minute/1.73 m 2 is not recommended.

renal_impairment.description: Assess eGFR prior to initiation and periodically thereafter. Contraindicated if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²; initiation not recommended if eGFR 30–45 mL/min/1.73 m². Discontinue at or prior to iodinated contrast imaging in patients with eGFR 30–60 mL/min/1.73 m², history of liver disease, alcoholism, heart failure, or intra-arterial contrast, and re-evaluate eGFR 48 hours later.

refs.locator: 2.3 Discontinuation for Iodinated Contrast Imaging Procedures
refs.quote: Discontinue GLUMETZA at the time of, or prior to, an iodinated contrast imaging procedure in patients with an eGFR between 30 and 60 mL/minute/1.73 m 2 ; in patients with a history of liver disease, alcoholism or heart failure; or in patients who will be administered intra-arterial iodinated contrast.

hemodialysis.value: Contraindicated in severe renal impairment (eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²). In overdose or metformin-associated lactic acidosis, metformin is dialyzable with a clearance of up to 170 mL/minute under good hemodynamic conditions; prompt hemodialysis is recommended.

refs.quote: Metformin is dialyzable with a clearance of up to 170 mL/minute under good hemodynamic conditions. Therefore, hemodialysis may be useful for removal of accumulated drug from patients in whom metformin overdosage is suspected.

hepatic.value: Not recommended / avoid use in patients with hepatic impairment; use of metformin in patients with hepatic impairment has been associated with cases of lactic acidosis.

refs.quote: Use of metformin in patients with hepatic impairment has been associated with some cases of lactic acidosis. GLUMETZA is not recommended in patients with hepatic impairment [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 )].

value: LACTIC ACIDOSIS: Postmarketing cases of metformin-associated lactic acidosis have resulted in death, hypothermia, hypotension, and resistant bradyarrhythmias. Risk factors include renal impairment, concomitant use of certain drugs (e.g., carbonic anhydrase inhibitors such as topiramate), age >=65 years, radiological studies with contrast, surgery, hypoxic states, excessive alcohol intake, hepatic impairment, and mitochondrial diseases. If suspected, immediately discontinue and institute supportive measures; prompt hemodialysis is recommended.

If metformin-associated lactic acidosis is suspected, immediately discontinue GLUMETZA and institute general supportive measures in a hospital setting. Prompt hemodialysis is recommended [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 )].

mechanism_of_action.value: Biguanide antihyperglycemic agent that decreases hepatic glucose production, decreases intestinal absorption of glucose, and improves insulin sensitivity by increasing peripheral glucose uptake and utilization; insulin secretion remains unchanged.

refs.quote: Metformin decreases hepatic glucose production, decreases intestinal absorption of glucose, and improves insulin sensitivity by increasing peripheral glucose uptake and utilization. With metformin therapy, insulin secretion remains unchanged while fasting insulin levels and day-long plasma insulin response may decrease.

value.metabolism: Excreted unchanged in the urine; does not undergo hepatic metabolism nor biliary excretion; eliminated via renal tubular secretion (OCT2/MATE).

refs.quote: Intravenous, single-dose studies in healthy subjects demonstrate that metformin is excreted unchanged in the urine and does not undergo hepatic metabolism (no metabolites have been identified in humans), nor biliary excretion.

value.drug_or_class: Carbonic Anhydrase Inhibitors (Topiramate, Zonisamide, Acetazolamide, Dichlorphenamide)
value.effect: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors frequently cause decreased serum bicarbonate and non-anion gap, hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis; concomitant use may increase the risk for lactic acidosis.
value.management: Consider more frequent monitoring of these patients.

refs.quote: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors frequently cause a decrease in serum bicarbonate and induce non-anion gap, hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis. Concomitant use of these drugs with GLUMETZA may increase the risk for lactic acidosis. Intervention: Consider more frequent monitoring of these patients. Examples: Topiramate, zonisamide, acetazolamide or dichlorphenamide.

value.drug_or_class: Drugs that Reduce Metformin Clearance (OCT2/MATE Inhibitors: Ranolazine, Vandetanib, Dolutegravir, Cimetidine)
value.effect: Interferes with renal tubular transport systems involved in metformin elimination, increasing systemic exposure to metformin and risk for lactic acidosis.
value.management: Consider the benefits and risks of concomitant use with GLUMETZA.

refs.quote: Concomitant use of drugs that interfere with common renal tubular transport systems involved in the renal elimination of metformin (e.g., organic cationic transporter-2 [OCT2] / multidrug and toxin extrusion [MATE] inhibitors) could increase systemic exposure to metformin and may increase the risk for lactic acidosis

value.effect: Alcohol potentiates the effect of metformin on lactate metabolism, increasing lactic acidosis risk.
value.management: Warn patients against excessive alcohol intake while receiving GLUMETZA.

refs.quote: Alcohol Clinical Impact: Alcohol is known to potentiate the effect of metformin on lactate metabolism. Intervention: Warn patients against excessive alcohol intake while receiving GLUMETZA.

value.effect: Coadministration with an insulin secretagogue (e.g., sulfonylurea) or insulin may increase the risk of hypoglycemia.
value.management: Patients receiving an insulin secretagogue or insulin may require lower doses of the insulin secretagogue or insulin.

value.effect: Certain drugs tend to produce hyperglycemia and may lead to loss of glycemic control.
value.management: Observe patient closely for loss of blood glucose control when administered, and for hypoglycemia when withdrawn.

refs.quote: Certain drugs tend to produce hyperglycemia and may lead to loss of glycemic control. Intervention: When such drugs are administered to a patient receiving GLUMETZA, observe the patient closely for loss of blood glucose control. When such drugs are withdrawn from a patient receiving GLUMETZA, observe the patient closely for hypoglycemia.
